name: Windows Terminal

verifiedAgainst.note: Every default chord was read from the defaults.json that ships inside the installed package, plus the first-run user template embedded in Microsoft.Terminal.Settings.Model.dll. Cross-checked against the Learn docs and upstream main (identical keybindings; main only adds an unbound Terminal.Workspaces action). 1.25.2733.0 is the current stable release (2026-10-02); 1.26.2734.0 is Preview.

policy.reason: Ordinary desktop app; every default is a documented shortcut, so Sight is not needed.

any.note: Executable named in the package AppxManifest (S9). Also the host when Windows Terminal is the default terminal app, so cmd/pwsh started from anywhere land here.
Package family from Get-AppxPackage + Application Id=App from the manifest (S9).
Preview package family per the Learn settings path (S5); Application Id assumed to be App like stable. Preview isn't installed here.
Top-level window class from the Terminal source, IslandWindow.cpp (S8). Not observed live: no Terminal window was open during the probe.

contexts.label: Mark mode (keyboard selection)

any.note: Planned probe: UIA TextPattern selection on the focused TermControl. Fallback: the engine enters this context after our own sel.markMode press and leaves on Enter, Esc, a copy, or a focus change.

contexts.verify: With Accessibility Insights on WT 1.25, press Ctrl+Shift+M and check whether the TermControl's TextPattern.GetSelection returns a non-empty range (or a selection-marker element appears). If nothing is exposed, use the engine-tracked fallback and say so in the PI.
contexts.notes: The title bar doesn't change in mark mode, so there's no windowTitle detector. The mark-mode keys themselves (arrows, Enter, Tab) are fixed by the Terminal and can't be rebound (S4).

verbs.label: LAST TAB
verbs.notes: Ctrl+Alt+9 is the last tab, not tab 9 (index 4294967295 in defaults.json).

verbs.label: PROFILE 1
verbs.longLabel: New tab with the first profile in the dropdown
verbs.notes: Ctrl+Shift+1..9 = profiles 1..9 in dropdown order. The profile name isn't in defaults; reading the user's profiles list for a label would expose profile names, so keep the generic label.

verbs.label: REOPEN
verbs.longLabel: Restore the last closed tab or pane

unavailable.label: BIND ME
unavailable.hint: Reopen has no default key: add one in Settings > Actions (Restore the last closed pane or tab).

verbs.label: SPLIT RIGHT
verbs.longLabel: Split pane to the right (duplicate profile)

binding.note: defaults.json says alt+shift+plus; 'plus' is the main-row =/+ key.

verbs.label: SPLIT AUTO
verbs.longLabel: Duplicate pane, Terminal picks the direction
verbs.conflict: Not in defaults.json (S1). Alt+Shift+D comes from the first-run user template (S2/S7) that Terminal writes into a new settings.json; Learn (S5) documents it as a default. A settings.json created before the template or edited by hand may not have it.
verbs.notes: Read the user's keybindings: if no entry binds Terminal.DuplicatePaneAuto, show the unavailable face with a bind hint.

verbs.label: CLOSE PANE
verbs.longLabel: Close the focused pane (ends its shell)
verbs.notes: Hold to confirm: it ends whatever is running in the pane. The last pane closes the tab. closeTab (no confirmation, all panes) is deliberately unbound in defaults.json.

unavailable.label: BIND ME
unavailable.hint: Pane zoom has no default key: add one in Settings > Actions (Toggle pane zoom).

verbs.label: BROADCAST
verbs.longLabel: Toggle broadcast input to all panes in the tab

unavailable.label: BIND ME
unavailable.hint: Broadcast input has no default key: add one in Settings > Actions.

verbs.label: FIND
verbs.notes: Next/previous match (Terminal.FindNextMatch / FindPrevMatch) have no default key; inside the search box Enter / Shift+Enter step through matches.

verbs.label: FULLSCREEN
verbs.notes: No state readout yet: the windows module could report it (window rect == monitor rect, no caption).

unavailable.label: BIND ME
unavailable.hint: Focus mode has no default key: add one in Settings > Actions.

verbs.label: ON TOP
verbs.longLabel: Keep this Terminal window on top

unavailable.label: ON TOP
unavailable.hint: Needs the Prism Control windows module.

verbs.notes: Terminal's own toggleAlwaysOnTop has no default key. If the user binds one, Prism presses it (keeps Terminal's internal flag in sync) and still reads the true state from the module. Setting TOPMOST from outside can drift from Terminal's own flag; verify.

verbs.label: QUAKE

binding.note: defaults.json binds win+sc(41): scan code 41 is the key left of 1 on a US layout. On layouts where that key isn't VK_OEM_3, send the scan code.

unavailable.label: QUAKE
unavailable.hint: Windows Terminal isn't running, so its global quake hotkey isn't registered.

verbs.notes: A global hotkey (globalSummon) while any WindowsTerminal.exe runs, not only when Terminal is in front. The schema can't say 'global while the process runs'; contexts '*' is the closest.

verbs.label: SUGGEST
verbs.notes: Command history in suggestions needs shell integration enabled in the profile.

verbs.label: CLOSE WIN
verbs.notes: Ends every shell in the window; Terminal only asks first when confirmCloseAllTabs is on.

verbs.label: COPY

altBindings.note: First-run user template (S2); only copies when text is selected, otherwise it's the shell's interrupt.

unavailable.label: COPY
unavailable.hint: Select text first (mouse, or MARK MODE).

verbs.notes: Never send Ctrl+C as the primary: with no selection it interrupts the running program. Enter also copies when a selection exists (defaults.json).

verbs.label: PASTE
verbs.notes: Multi-line pastes may trigger Terminal's paste warning.

verbs.label: MARK MODE
verbs.longLabel: Toggle mark mode (select with the keyboard)

verbs.label: BLOCK SEL
verbs.longLabel: Turn the selection into a block (rectangle)

unavailable.label: BIND ME
unavailable.hint: Block selection has no default key: add one in Settings > Actions. (Alt+drag with the mouse also works.)

verbs.label: OTHER END
verbs.longLabel: Switch which end of the selection moves

unavailable.label: BIND ME
unavailable.hint: Switch selection endpoint has no default key: add one in Settings > Actions.

verbs.label: COPY SEL
verbs.longLabel: Copy the selection (Enter in mark mode)

unavailable.label: COPY SEL
unavailable.hint: Only in mark mode with a selection.

verbs.notes: Enter is bound to Terminal.CopyToClipboard in defaults.json and only acts when a selection exists; otherwise it reaches the shell. That's why this verb lives only in markMode.

verbs.label: CLEAR SEL
verbs.longLabel: Clear the selection / leave mark mode
verbs.notes: Fixed key, not an action; no appAction to rebind.

verbs.label: NEXT LINK
verbs.longLabel: Jump to the next hyperlink in the buffer
verbs.notes: Fixed key. URL detection needs experimental.detectUrls on.

verbs.label: TOP
verbs.longLabel: Scroll to the top of the buffer

verbs.label: CLEAR
verbs.notes: Scrollback can't be recovered; only a direct press runs it.

verbs.label: FONT +
verbs.notes: For key-only decks; the fontSize dial is the main control.

controls.label: TABS
controls.notes: No acceleration: a big spin shouldn't fly past the tab you want. The tab-switcher popup may appear if tabSwitcherMode is on; each press still moves one tab.

controls.label: SCROLL

step.note: scrollUp/scrollDown without rowsToScroll move the system mouse-wheel amount (usually 3 lines). Big spins switch to page steps via acceleration below.

controls.notes: Page steps are Ctrl+Shift+PageUp / PageDown (Terminal.ScrollUpPage / ScrollDownPage). The schema has one left/right binding per dial, so a 'switch to page steps on fast spins' rule can't be written; acceleration repeats the line step instead.

controls.label: FONT SIZE
controls.notes: Font zoom is per-pane and isn't saved. The clamp is on our counted steps from the profile's size, not absolute points (we don't read the profile font size).

controls.label: PANE SIZE

step.note: Terminal moves the split by a fixed share per press; exact amount not documented.

unavailable.label: PANE SIZE
unavailable.hint: Needs two panes side by side.

controls.notes: Vertical resizing (Alt+Shift+Up/Down) is the same pattern; a second dial layer could carry it.

controls.label: PANES

step.note: Directional: moves to the neighbor on that side, if any.

controls.notes: Cycling in order (Terminal.MoveFocusNextInOrder / PreviousInOrder) would suit a dial better but has no default key.

readouts.label: TAB

source.note: Foreground window title = the active tab's title (shell/app-set, often the running command or a path).

readouts.notes: Titles can show paths, hostnames and user names; streamer-safe shows 'Terminal' only.

readouts.label: SCROLLED

source.note: Our own presses since the last scroll-to-bottom; typing in the shell also snaps back, which we can't see.

readouts.verify: Check whether a UIA ScrollPattern on the TermControl exposes VerticalScrollPercent; if so switch this to a module readout.

source.note: Counted from the profile size; font.reset should zero it.

readouts.label: MARK

source.note: Same signal as the markMode detector.

readouts.verify: See the markMode context's verify step.

userBindings.summary: Rebinds live in settings.json (JSONC). Since 1.21 actions and keys are split: 'actions' define commands with an id, 'keybindings' map keys to an id. Older files put 'keys' inside each action (or in a legacy 'keybindings' list of command+keys); Terminal migrates them when it next saves. Layering: shipped defaults.json, then fragments, then settings.json (later wins per key).

locations.note: Stable (Store). Present on this PC; uses the 1.21+ split format.
Canary; package family by analogy, unverified.
Unpackaged installs (Scoop, Chocolatey, zip) per Learn.
Portable mode (a .portable marker file next to the exe); unverified here.
Shipped defaults (readable without admin). Read it to refresh this pack when Terminal updates; never edit.

userBindings.entryShape: 1.21+: actions[] = { command: string | { action, ...args }, id: 'User.<name>', name?, icon? }; keybindings[] = { keys: string | string[], id: '<action id>' | null | 'unbound' }. Join: a keybindings entry whose id equals the verb's appAction (Terminal.*), or whose id names a user action whose command+args equal the default command behind that appAction. id null or 'unbound' removes the default key. Legacy (pre-1.21): actions[] = { command, keys } with no id; match by command+args against defaults.json.
userBindings.keyNameMap: Lower-case, '+'-joined, any modifier order (normalize to Win, Ctrl, Alt, Shift). 'plus' and '=' = Equal; '-' = Minus; ',' = Comma; '.' or 'period' = Period; '`' = Backquote; 'sc(N)' = scan code N (sc(41) = Backquote position); pgup/pageup = PageUp; pgdn/pagedown = PageDown; app/menu = ContextMenu; esc/escape = Esc; numpad_plus/numpad_add = NumpadAdd; numpad_minus/numpad_subtract = NumpadSubtract; numpad_0..9 or numpad0..9 = Numpad0..9; numpad_period/numpad_decimal = NumpadDecimal; f1..f24, a..z, 0..9 as is.
userBindings.readMode: Read-only. Strip comments and trailing commas, then parse. Watch the file (FileSystemWatcher); Terminal itself rewrites it on launch or save, so debounce about 500 ms and re-read. If parsing fails, keep the defaults and say so in the PI. Never write to it.
userBindings.verify: Fragments can add actions in recent builds (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows Terminal\Fragments\<app>\*.json, which exists here): confirm whether fragment actions can carry keys, and include them in the layering if so.

layouts.rationale: New tab, split and palette on top; copy/paste/find and modes in the middle; the hold-to-confirm and never-auto keys at the bottom, away from the top row; tabs and scroll on layer 0 since they're used most.
In mark mode the dials grow the selection by lines and words, a push copies (left) or clears (right), and the keys cover links and block selection.
Top row is create/find, bottom row is the clipboard plus mark mode, with close pane in the far corner; all four dials carry continuous controls and the strip shows tab, scroll and font.
Same as the Galleon mark-mode page: copy and clear at the ends of the top row, links below, and selection growth on the first two dials.

conflicts: Alt+Shift+D (duplicate pane, auto direction): Learn (S5) lists it as a default, but defaults.json (S1/S6) doesn't bind it. It comes from the first-run user template (S2/S7), so it exists only if the user's settings.json still has that entry.
Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V: not in defaults.json (S1); seeded by the user template (S2). Ctrl+Shift+C/V and Ctrl+Insert/Shift+Insert are the true defaults.
Alt+Space: Terminal binds it to the system menu (S1/S3), but the Copilot app (S11) and PowerToys Run (default hotkey) register it globally, and both are installed and enabled here.
Learn's actions page (S3) prints the defaultsFile entry with a stray "keys" where "id" belongs (a doc typo); defaults.json (S1) has id Terminal.OpenDefaultSettingsFile.
gaps: Mark-mode detection has no confirmed signal (UIA probe planned).
No true readouts for tab count/index, fullscreen, focus mode, broadcast or pane zoom; the window title is the only live text, and it's streamer-hidden.
Scroll position is only our own counted presses; typing snaps the view back without us seeing it.
Profile names for PROFILE 1 aren't shown (privacy and no stable read path); the keys say PROFILE n.
Quake mode is a global hotkey while Terminal runs; the schema can't scope a verb to 'any foreground while process X runs'.
notes: Orca (the user's Electron agent IDE) also hosts terminals, but it's out of scope here: it needs its own pack (Chrome_WidgetWin_1 window class, Orca.exe).
Keep this pack in sync by diffing the installed defaults.json after each Terminal update (the package folder name carries the version).

Also bound by default but not drawn as verbs (kept out to stay near 40): Ctrl+Alt+3..8 (tabs 3-8), Ctrl+Shift+2..9 (profiles 2-9), Ctrl+Shift+N (new window), Ctrl+Shift+Comma / Ctrl+Alt+Comma (open settings.json / defaults.json), Alt+Shift+arrows (resize pane; on the paneSize dial), Ctrl+Shift+PageUp/PageDown (page scroll), Alt+Space (system menu; see conflicts), Menu key (context menu). Unbound actions not drawn: rename tab, tab color, export buffer, close other tabs/panes, swap/move pane, read-only mode, open CWD, quick fix.
Verbs with no default key are shown as BIND ME with a suggested chord taken from unused Ctrl+Alt+Shift space; if the user binds them, Prism picks up the chord from settings.json through appAction.
